title: 赴英留学生的残酷现实（5）
desc: 赴英留学生的残酷现实（5）

paragraphs.en: A quick search on Instagram turns up scores of videos offering advice on how to find a job, with titles such as "warehouses in the UK hiring now" or urging readers to comment to get tip sheets on finding part-time work.
paragraphs.zh: 在Instagram上快速搜索，就能找到大量关于如何找工作的视频，标题诸如“英国仓库现正招聘”或鼓励读者留言获取兼职工作指南。

paragraphs.en: "You're not behind," says one advice video. "You just need better directions." The message of these videos is that this is part of the hustle, and that it will all be worth it for a British degree.
paragraphs.zh: 一条建议视频说道：“你并没有落后，你只是需要更好的方向。”这些视频传达的信息是，这是奋斗的一部分，为了获得英国学位，这一切都是值得的。

paragraphs.en: "Go for the course, go for something you want to be in life," says one YouTuber as he chats to Indian students in Leicester about their studies and efforts to find part-time work. "I say every time, don't give up. You have to go again, go again, go again."
paragraphs.zh: "去追求你的课程，去追求你人生中想做的事，"一位YouTube博主在莱斯特与印度学生聊到他们的学业和找兼职工作的努力时说道。"我每次都说，不要放弃。你必须一次又一次地去尝试，去尝试，去尝试。"

paragraphs.en: Sam graduated from Dundee in autumn 2024. His family couldn't afford to come to the UK for the ceremony, so he attended alone. He had enjoyed his master's degree in finance and felt well supported by the university's careers service.
paragraphs.zh: 萨姆于2024年秋季从邓迪大学毕业。由于家人无力承担赴英参加毕业典礼的费用，他独自一人出席了仪式。在攻读金融硕士学位期间，他非常享受学习过程，并感受到学校就业服务部门的有力支持。

paragraphs.en: But he was anxious about what would come next. He was still frantically filling out job applications. None were successful. Now he had finished his studies, he was no longer restricted to working 20 hours a week, so he took whatever shifts he could at the sweet shop and takeaway in Dundee where he regularly worked.
paragraphs.zh: 但他对接下来会发生什么感到焦虑。他仍在疯狂地投递工作申请，却无一成功。如今学业已结束，他不再受限于每周只能工作20小时的规定，于是在邓迪那家他经常打工的糖果店和外卖店，他尽可能地接下了所有能排到的班次。

paragraphs.en: Even for domestic graduates in the UK, the jobs market is bruisingly competitive: in 2024, employers reported 140 applications for every graduate vacancy.
paragraphs.zh: 甚至对英国本土毕业生而言，就业市场的竞争也异常激烈：2024年数据显示，雇主收到的每一份毕业生岗位申请都对应着140名竞争者。

paragraphs.en: For international students, it is even tougher. They must find an employer who is licensed to sponsor their visa, and since July 2025, anyone applying for a skilled worker visa must also earn at least £41,700.  Given that the median graduate starting salary is about £32,000, this is an extremely high bar.
paragraphs.zh: 对于国际学生来说，情况更加困难。他们必须找到一家有资格为其担保签证的雇主，而且自2025年7月起，申请技术工人签证的人还必须至少41,700英镑的年薪。考虑到毕业生的平均起薪约为32,000英镑，这一门槛显得极高。

paragraphs.en: In 2025, Janhavi Jain, a recent graduate from the Warwick Business School, posted on X: "I have tonnes of people text me about coming to the UK for master's, I will tell you to not come, 90% of my batch had to go back because there are no jobs, unless you have money to throw, don't consider it."
paragraphs.zh: 2025年，华威商学院应届毕业生贾纳维·贾恩在X平台上发文称：“好多人私信问我关于来英国读硕士的事，我的建议是别来——我们这届90%的同学因为找不到工作只能回国。除非你钱多得可以随便挥霍，否则别考虑这条路。”

paragraphs.en: The tweet struck a chord, getting hundreds of reposts and even a write-up by NDTV, a major Indian broadcaster. "The response was crazy," Jain told me. "I realised this was a universal experience."
paragraphs.zh: 这条推文引起了共鸣，获得了数百次转发，甚至得到了印度主要广播公司NDTV的专题报道。"反响太疯狂了，"贾因告诉我，"我意识到这是一种普遍的经历。"

paragraphs.en: For students from less prestigious universities, the route to a high-paying graduate job is even less clear. Ajith, the digital marketing student, spent every spare hour on the Aldi shop floor and had no time for the unpaid work experience that might have helped him build his CV.
paragraphs.zh: 对于来自非名校的学生而言，通往高薪毕业生职位的道路更加模糊。数字营销专业的学生阿吉斯将所有课余时间都花在阿尔迪超市的货架间，无暇参与那些或许能为简历增色的无薪实习。

paragraphs.en: "I'm doing one job, which makes it impossible to get the other kind of job," he said. Four months after finishing his master's, he returned to Tamil Nadu. He now works as a supervisor at a factory near his family home, earning £300 per month. "I had a lot of dreams, but everything was spoiled," he told me. "I came back with a broken heart."
paragraphs.zh: "我干着这份工作，就没法再找其他类型的工作了，"他说道。完成硕士学位四个月后，他回到了泰米尔纳德邦。如今，他在家乡附近的工厂担任主管，月薪300英镑。"我原本有很多梦想，但一切都毁了，"他告诉我，"我是带着破碎的心回来的。"

paragraphs.en: Sam continued to stick it out in the UK, but his costs were mounting. In the spring of 2025, six months after graduation, the fixed loan repayments of £300 per month kicked in. He needed extra work, and through friends, found shifts at a vegetable packing factory on Dundee's outskirts, washing and packaging vegetables for Tesco and Aldi.
paragraphs.zh: 萨姆继续留在英国坚持着，但生活开销不断攀升。2025年春天，毕业六个月后，每月300英镑的固定贷款还款开始了。他需要额外的工作，通过朋友介绍，在邓迪郊区的蔬菜包装厂找到了轮班工作，为乐购和阿尔迪超市清洗包装蔬菜。

paragraphs.en: The commute was an hour and a half on public transport, so he split the taxi fare with a group of other students and recent graduates who were doing the same job. He worked 10-hour shifts at minimum wage. "By that time, my ego had died, so I had accepted: OK, we can do this," he told me.
paragraphs.zh: 通勤时间在公共交通上需要一个半小时，因此他与一群做着同样工作的其他学生和刚毕业的年轻人分摊了出租车费。他拿着最低工资，每天工作10小时。他告诉我：“那时我的自尊心已经消失殆尽，所以我接受了现实：好吧，我们可以这样做。”

paragraphs.en: Sam's total income was between £1,200 and £1,600 per month, depending on how many shifts he got. Most of the money went on rent and loan repayments. When his family in India asked how the job hunt was going, he got angry. He kept applying for corporate jobs but it was hard to stay hopeful.
paragraphs.zh: 萨姆每月的总收入在 1200 英镑到 1600 英镑之间，这取决于他能获得多少班次的工作。大部分钱都用于支付房租和贷款还款。当他身在印度的家人询问他的求职进展时，他非常生气。他一直在申请企业职位，但很难保持乐观的态度。
